population: 5930 patients with probable or definite Alzheimer's disease and 8607 controls without dementia from 40 research teams (clinical, community and brain-bank sources); Caucasian, African American, Hispanic and Japanese subjects (from the abstract)
conclusion: Against e3/e3, Caucasian clinic- and autopsy-based series gave OR 0.6 for e2/e2 (not significant) and e2/e3, 2.6 for e2/e4, 3.2 for e3/e4 and 14.9 for e4/e4. The e4 association was weaker in African American and Hispanic subjects and stronger in Japanese subjects. Supports the ordering of risk across the six genotypes and that effects vary by ancestry.
provenance_quote: Among Caucasian subjects from clinic- or autopsy-based studies, the risk of AD was significantly increased for people with genotypes epsilon2/epsilon4 (OR=2.6, 95% CI=1.6-4.0), epsilon3/epsilon4 (OR=3.2, 95% CI=2.8-3.8), and epsilon4/epsilon4 (OR=14.9, 95% CI= 10.8-20.6)

population: 42 families with late-onset Alzheimer's disease (from the abstract)
conclusion: Risk rose from 20% to 90% and mean age at onset fell from 84 to 68 years with the number of e4 alleles. Supports the gene-dose effect of e4 and earlier onset in e4/e4.
provenance_quote: Risk for AD increased from 20% to 90% and mean age at onset decreased from 84 to 68 years with increasing number of APOE-epsilon 4 alleles in 42 families with late onset AD.

population: 115 sporadic AD cases and 243 controls, plus 150 affected and 197 unaffected members of 66 AD families (from the abstract)
conclusion: Reported a protective effect of the e2 allele beside the dose effect of e4; risk was lowest in e2/e3. The original report of e2 protection.
provenance_quote: Our data demonstrate a protective effect of the epsilon 2 allele, in addition to the dose effect of the epsilon 4 allele in sporadic AD.

population: 68,756 individuals: 34,021 non-Hispanic White, 7,145 non-Hispanic Black and 5,738 Hispanic participants from case-control, family-based, population-based and longitudinal AD genetic cohorts, plus 21,852 East Asian individuals (Japan and Korea) from published summary statistics
conclusion: Against e3/e3 in White individuals: e2/e2 OR 0.39, e2/e3 0.53, e2/e4 2.23, e3/e4 3.46, e4/e4 13.04. e3/e4 was 4.54 in East Asian, 2.18 in Black and 1.90 in Hispanic individuals; e4/e4 was 6.49 in Black and 3.62 in Hispanic individuals. e2 was not associated with AD risk in Hispanic or East Asian individuals, and e2/e2 and e2/e4 did not reach significance in Hispanic individuals. Supports the size of each genotype's effect and its dependence on ancestry.
provenance_quote: Odds ratios for APOE *34 and AD risk attenuated following East Asian (OR, 4.54; 95% CI, 3.99-5.17), White (OR, 3.46; 95% CI, 3.27-3.65), Black (OR, 2.18; 95% CI, 1.90-2.49), and Hispanic (OR, 1.90; 95% CI, 1.65-2.18) individuals.

population: 7,531 AD cases and 10,132 controls, all Caucasian, from Spain, Finland, France, Italy, Belgium and the USA
conclusion: Modelled lifetime risk of AD by age 85, conditional on surviving to 85 (case-control genotype effects applied to Rochester incidence data and US life tables): about 8% (men) and 10% (women) for e3/e3, 20% and 27% for e2/e4, 23% and 30% for e3/e4, 51% (95% CI 41-70) and 60% (95% CI 47-84) for e4/e4, and 5% and 6% for e2/e2 plus e2/e3 together. With PAQUID (France) incidence data, e4/e4 women reach 68%. Pooled ORs against e3/e3: 14.49 for e4/e4, 3.63 for e3/e4, 2.64 for e2/e4, 0.56 for e2/e2 plus e2/e3. States that roughly 2% of Caucasians carry e4/e4 and that e4 is probably the ancestral allele. Source of the natural frequencies in the conclusions.
provenance_quote: At age 85, AD-LTR reached 51 % (95%CI= [41;70]) and 60% (95%CI= [47;84]) for APOE 44 male and female carriers respectively and 23% (95%CI= [22;25]) and 30% (95%CI= [28;32]) for APOE 34 male and female carriers respectively

population: More than 5,000 clinically and neuropathologically characterized non-Hispanic White Alzheimer's dementia cases and controls, compared with more than 24,000 clinically characterized cases and controls without neuropathology
conclusion: In the neuropathologically confirmed group e2/e2 had an OR of 0.13 against e3/e3; in the clinical group 0.52. Supports e2/e2 carrying the lowest APOE-related risk, with an uncertain exact size.
provenance_quote: an extremely low 0.13 OR (95% CI = 0.05–0.36) compared to the most common APOE3/3 genotype

population: 337,484 white British UK Biobank participants aged 37 to 73 years
conclusion: Genotype frequencies: e3/e3 58.2%, e3/e4 23.9%, e2/e3 12.3%, e2/e4 2.6%, e4/e4 2.4%, e2/e2 0.6%. Source of the population frequencies in the conclusions.

population: Narrative review of familial dysbetalipoproteinaemia and the APOE variants reported to cause it
conclusion: About 90% of familial dysbetalipoproteinaemia is e2/e2 homozygosity, but only 10-15% of e2/e2 carriers develop it, usually with an additional metabolic stress such as obesity, insulin resistance or diabetes. It presents as mixed hyperlipidaemia, carries a very high risk of premature atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, and lipid-lowering treatment is important.

population: 453,437 UK Biobank participants; dysbetalipoproteinaemia defined as an e2/e2 genotype with mixed dyslipidaemia or lipid-lowering therapy (n = 964) (from the abstract)
conclusion: 0.6% of participants were e2/e2, and 36% of them met the study's definition of dysbetalipoproteinaemia, a prevalence of 0.2% (1 in 469), similar across genetic ancestries. The upper end of the penetrance range in the e2/e2 conclusion, under a broad definition.
provenance_quote: Overall, 0.6% of participants had an ε2ε2 genotype, of which 36% were classified as DBL, for a disease prevalence of 0.2% (1:469).

population: 3,297 individuals in the pathology study and 10,039 in the clinical study, from the National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center and five large biomarker cohorts (from the abstract)
conclusion: Nearly all e4/e4 carriers showed Alzheimer's pathology and abnormal biomarkers from about age 55 to 65 (near-full penetrance of AD biology), and symptom onset was earlier, at a mean age of 65.1, than in e3/e3. Supports earlier onset in e4/e4 and the statement that nearly all e4/e4 carriers show the disease's brain changes by their mid-60s.
provenance_quote: The age of symptom onset was earlier in APOE4 homozygotes at 65.1, with a narrower 95% prediction interval than APOE3 homozygotes.

population: Expert-panel appropriate use recommendations for lecanemab, drawing on the CLARITY AD trial in early Alzheimer's disease
conclusion: APOE e4 carriers, especially homozygotes, are at higher risk of amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (brain swelling or microbleeds) on lecanemab, and APOE genotyping of treatment candidates is recommended to inform risk discussions. Source of the practical note on antibody medicines.
provenance_quote: Patients who are apolipoprotein E ε4 (APOE4) gene carriers, especially APOE4 homozygotes, are at higher risk for ARIA, and the AUR recommends APOE genotyping to better inform risk discussions with patients who are lecanemab candidates.
